verdicts.trueWording: one-off POV chapters feel so hobbled by their brevity
verdicts.note: Raw page (curl, browser UA, HTTP 200). Verbatim: 'Perhaps my problem with these one-off POV chapters is that they just feel so hobbled by their brevity.' Second limb also verbatim: 'we should be given characters who we've been reading about for four books already, not new characters.' Byline E.D./Erik Kain, August 8, 2011.

verdicts.trueWording: oscillates wildly between excellent North chapters and boredom
verdicts.note: Raw page. Verbatim: 'It oscillates wildly between excellent chapters in the North to some of the most boring moments in any fantasy series I've ever read'. Dany limb verbatim too: 'Daenerys's chapters...They were awful. They hurt the books.'

verdicts.trueWording: almost everything could have been written as hearsay
verdicts.note: Raw page. In the Daenerys paragraph: 'Dany's choices are bizarre... Almost everything that happens could have been written as hearsay in other POV characters' chapters and it would have been far more interesting.' Both limbs (hearsay route, more interesting) verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: cartoon villain, very real victims, truly disturbing torture
verdicts.note: Raw page. 'Sure, Ramsay Bolton is a cartoon villain, but his victims are very real' and, same paragraph, 'The torture in the books is truly disturbing, as it should be.' All three limbs verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: flagons 'n' dragons quoted, Jennings says 'much better'
verdicts.note: Raw page. Kain block-quotes Jennings ('has its share of flagons 'n' dragons, and swords 'n' sorcerers') and mocks it: 'There is no quicker way to the heart of a fantasy reader than to turn a phrase like flagons 'n' dragons in your opening paragraph, believe me. Ugh.' The 'much better' limb is explicit: 'Dana Jennings of the New York Times... going so far as to say that Martin is "much better" than Tolkien.'

verdicts.trueWording: instead of focusing, the story adds POVs and conflicts
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture 20160722111429id_ (live thinkprogress.org is dead). Verbatim opening of the paragraph; the paragraph enumerates the added plots (Aegon, Davos/Rickon, Mance, the Horn, sellswords) and closes 'It's exhausting.' — so the 'exhausting' limb is supported as the paragraph's own summing-up.

verdicts.trueWording: we're tangled up in a comparative anthropology of sellswords
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture. Verbatim: 'We're tangled up in a comparative anthropology of sellsword companies. It's exhausting.'

verdicts.trueWording: constant punning on Reek irritates but shows the reinforcement
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture. Verbatim: 'The constant punning on Reek, the name Ramsay gives Theon, can be irritating, but it's also an illustration of how difficult it is to brainwash yourself into being another person, how constant that reinforcement must have to be.' Page hedges 'can be irritating' where the claim says 'is irritating' — a softening, not a mismatch.

verdicts.trueWording: cartoon psychopath, effective because seen from his victim
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture. Verbatim: 'Ramsay Snow's a cartoon psychopath, but a genuinely effective one for all of that because we see him from the perspective of someone he's systematically broken down and built up into a new creation.' Page names him Ramsay Snow (pre-legitimisation), claim says 'Ramsay'.

verdicts.trueWording: three main characters forget their names and learn new ones
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture. Verbatim: 'As the three main characters in the novel who have to forget their names and learn new ones, Theon exchanges his sense of self for survival, Arya learns to wear many names and many faces..., and in trading his true name for a false one, Tyrion Lannister begins an extended meditation on who he truly is.' Page says 'three main characters'; 'separate viewpoints' is the analyst's word, but all three are POV characters and the same post discusses the book's added points of view.

verdicts.trueWording: I could acknowledge the plotty, cliffhangery aspects as a selling point
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture of tigerbeatdown.com (live host refuses connection). Quote and the whole reversal list are verbatim: 'I could acknowledge the plotty, cliffhangery aspects of Martin's writing as a selling point: So-and-so was dead! But now he's alive! But now he's dying! But now he's a zombie! But now he's the Prince of Sblarghlhaar, because he was IN DISGUISE!' But it sits in a run of declined moves ('I could get into the reasons... I could try to construct some kind of nuanced argument... I could try to look at the positives, before I get to the criticism. But you know what? I'm still going to criticize the books'), so the concession is hypothetical and withheld, and the article is 'a selling point', not 'the'.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: conceded as the selling point — the page frames it as a hypothetical 'I could acknowledge... as a selling point' that Doyle then declines

verdicts.trueWording: in days of yore, before the Striding Elves sailed West
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture. The sentence opens the post's second paragraph, directly under 'George R.R. Martin is creepy. / There! I said it!' Faux-archaic register and unpronounceable names both present: 'Sygmagfhdflkglll', 'the mighty Tghfarghfr Mountains', and 'yon Good Queen Sady' verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: she gets kidnapped, escapes, runs away — on a loop
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture. Verbatim loop: 'She gets kidnapped! She escapes! She runs away! She gets kidnapped! She escapes! She runs away!... Then she gets kidnapped! WILL SHE ESCAPE? Yes!' and the section heading is verbatim '2. A Clash of Kings, or, The One That Was Really Boring'.

verdicts.trueWording: Other-ized names like Pyat, Xaro Xhoan, Jhogo vs Ned, Catelyn, Jon
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture. Verbatim: 'they all have racialized/Other-ized names like "Pyat," "Xaro Xhoan," and "Jhogo," as opposed to Dragon Land names like "Ned," "Catelyn," and "Jon."' The page's satirical term for Westeros is 'Dragon Land' (used the same way at 'When last we visited Mystical Dragon Land'), so 'Westerosi' is a gloss on her wording, not an addition.

verdicts.trueWording: creepy primarily for his gratuitous rape/molestation/DV scenes
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture. The core-objection limb is verbatim: 'He is creepy, primarily, because of his TWENTY THOUSAND MILLION GRATUITOUS RAPE AND/OR MOLESTATION AND/OR DOMESTIC VIOLENCE SCENES. And I could write a post about those... But you know what would be easier? I could just count them. One by one by one.' The essay does walk the books in order (sections 1-4, each with a 'Major Female Characters' roster), but no per-book count of scenes exists: the arithmetic is one cumulative 'FINAL SCORES' block after book four counting characters, not scenes — '83%' of major female characters abused/raped/threatened, '100%' of the female children.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: tallied book by book — the tallies are a single cumulative FINAL SCORES block (percentages of major female characters), not a per-book count of scenes
